remittance

rih-MIT-unss · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Remittance is a sum of money sent, often to another person or place.

The small village depended heavily on remittances sent home by relatives working abroad in the capital.

Example

After finding steady work in the city, the young man began sending a monthly remittance to cover his younger siblings' school fees back home.

A remittance is money sent from one place to another, most often support sent home to family.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

payment: A payment is money handed over because something is owed -- for a purchase, a bill, or a debt. A remittance settles nothing: it is money sent, usually across a distance, and most often it is support -- earnings passed along to family far away.

transfer: A transfer is the bare movement of money from one account or person to another -- pure mechanics, saying nothing about why. Remittance adds the why and the where: it is money sent to someone at a distance, classically a worker's support for family back home.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

withdrawal: the act of taking money out rather than sending it

debt: money owed rather than sent

Where it sits · how large and lasting the payment is

gift → remittance → endowment

gift vs. remittance: A gift is a one-time act of giving with no schedule behind it, while a remittance usually arrives again and again, sent on purpose to support someone.

endowment vs. remittance: An endowment is a large, often permanent sum set aside for continuous support -- far more substantial than a routine remittance.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — re-: back (Latin)

root — mitt-: to send (from Latin mittere)

suffix — -ance: the act or result of; forms a noun (Latin)

Put it together: Remittance is built from re- ('back') + mitt- ('to send,' from Latin mittere) + -ance (a noun ending) -- literally 'a sending back,' which is exactly what a remittance is: money sent back home or to someone else.

Use the root in a new word: transmit: Certain mosquitoes can transmit the illness after a single bite.

Word Choice

Remittance is most common in economic and financial contexts -- news articles often discuss 'remittances' sent home by workers living abroad. Compare it with remunerate, the verb for paying someone directly for work they've done.
